$schema_note: SYNTHETIC DEMO DATA. Work IQ email corpus for the Capital Markets Client Intelligence Agent. BMO Capital Markets is a branding label only. Gibson Energy Inc. is a real public company, used only so the Web IQ layer's live grounding returns genuine public news - every internal figure, colleague, exposure, limit, covenant, approval and policy referenced here is invented for a demo. UPNs use the {TENANT_DOMAIN} placeholder which seed_work_iq.py substitutes from user_mapping.json. Every email carries a client_id giving the portfolio client it belongs to (CLI-1001 Gibson Energy Inc., CLI-1002 Keyera Corp., CLI-1007 Cascades Inc.); consumers match on that field rather than on the company name appearing in the text.
scenario: BMO Capital Markets - preparation for the 13 August 2026 Gibson Energy (TSX:GEI) CFO/Treasurer coverage meeting

people.title: Executive Director, Equity Research - Energy Infrastructure

emails.subject: Gibson Energy FY26 account plan - signed off, and what I want from H2
emails.body:
Team,

I signed the FY26 account plan for Gibson Energy this morning. It is filed in the coverage channel. Three things I want everyone carrying into the second half.

First, we have earned the right to ask for more. FY26 year to date revenue is CAD 8.42m against CAD 7.14m in the same period last year, up 17.9 per cent. Estimated wallet share is 21.4 per cent, up from 18.9, and we have moved from third to second. That is the strongest relationship trajectory in my book and it is almost entirely down to the July note offering and the Chauvin bridge take-out.

Second, we are strong in the wrong places to be comfortable. We are number one in commodity derivatives and nowhere in equity - zero revenue against an estimated CAD 2.8m of street wallet. M&A is CAD 0.45m against an estimated CAD 4.5m. We financed the Chauvin transaction; we did not advise on it. I do not want to be the balance sheet that funds someone else's advisory fee again.

Third, the three H2 objectives are the revolver upsize and extension, the hedging overlay on the Chauvin volumes, and positioning for the 2027 maturity. Sasha owns one and three, Quinn owns two, Vance is the control on all of them.

The CFO and Treasurer meeting is 13 August in Calgary. I want a pre-meeting brief that meets the CP-014 standard - every field populated, and where a field cannot be populated it says so rather than going quiet. Please do not send me a brief with the covenant line missing because it was awkward.

Sydney

emails.subject: Call report - Gibson Treasurer, 21 July
emails.body:
Sydney,

Call report filed, summary here.

Spoke with the Treasurer for forty minutes. Three things came out of it.

1. They want to talk about the revolver. Their words were that the facility is 'sized for the company we were, not the company we are'. They are thinking about moving the syndicate facility from CAD 1.10bn to somewhere around CAD 1.35bn and extending a year. They asked what our appetite would be at a larger hold. I said we would come back with an indication and that anything I gave them would be subject to internal approval - I was explicit about that and it is in the call report per CP-014.

2. They are unhappy with the differential exposure. Post-Chauvin they have more barrels touching the heavy-light differential than they are comfortable with and the Treasurer used the phrase 'we got the volume, we did not get the hedge'. That is Quinn's opening.

3. They asked, unprompted, whether we do sustainability-linked structures. They have no framework and no second-party opinion. I did not label anything - indicative discussion only, per CP-011.

One open commitment carried over from the 21 May meeting: we owed them a comparison of our cash management proposition against their incumbent. That is now nine weeks old and it is still open. I would rather close it before 13 August than have the CFO raise it.

Sasha

emails.subject: RE: Call report - Gibson Treasurer, 21 July - do not indicate a hold yet
emails.body:
Sasha,

Before you put any number in front of them, three constraints.

One. Our current hold is CAD 165m on the revolver. Total committed across all five facilities is CAD 465m, drawn CAD 288.4m, measured exposure CAD 341.7m against a CAD 500m single-name limit. That is 68.3 per cent - green, and there is headroom. But headroom is not authority. CP-001 is explicit on that.

Two. The Energy sector concentration limit is amber. We are at CAD 2,744m against a CAD 3,200m ceiling, 85.8 per cent. Under CP-002, any new commitment in the sector needs Portfolio Management sign-off and an identified offset, and the default expectation for a new lead-arranged position is that our final hold is materially below our arrangement position with the distribution plan documented before we commit, not after.

Three, and this is the one I care most about. Total Net Debt to Adjusted EBITDA sits at 4.18x against a 4.50x maximum. That is 0.32 turns of headroom. It is inside the Tight band under CP-005 - below 0.35 turns. It went the wrong way this quarter, from 3.94x, on a full quarter of Chauvin debt service. Because the transaction would complete within two quarters of a scheduled test date, CP-005 requires a pro-forma test signed off by Credit Risk before the pitch is delivered, on a fully drawn assumption. Not before mandate - before pitch.

I will have the pro-forma to you by 6 August. Please do not indicate a hold size before then.

Vance

emails.subject: Chauvin hedging overlay - shape of what I would put in front of them
emails.body:
Picking up the differential comment from Sasha's call report.

What I would propose is roughly CAD 240m notional over 24 months in two pieces: a WTI-WCS differential structure covering the incremental Chauvin barrels, and a CAD/USD forward strip against their USD revenue. Indicative revenue to us around CAD 0.94m over the life.

Three things I need before I can put anything in front of the Treasurer.

Documented underlying exposure. CP-010 says the exposure being hedged is documented before the structure is proposed - volume, tenor, benchmark, direction. I have their public volumes but not the contracted split, and I am not proposing a notional above documented exposure. If the incremental barrels are smaller than I think, the notional comes down.

Credit pre-clearance. Their derivative pre-settlement line is CAD 90m and we are using CAD 69.2m of it, so 77 per cent. A differential structure carries a higher potential future exposure add-on than an outright of the same notional under CP-004, because the spread distribution is fatter-tailed. I cannot quote a differential on an outright add-on. Vance, I need you to size this properly before I go anywhere near the client.

Tier 2 treatment. A differential swap is Tier 2 under CP-010 - written payoff illustration under at least three scenarios including the adverse case, and the adverse case has to include the differential moving against them while the outright moves in their favour. That is the scenario clients never expect and it is the one that generates the complaint.

We are number one in wallet on commodity derivatives with this client. That is the position I do not want to lose by rushing this.

Quinn

emails.subject: RE: Chauvin hedging overlay - PSE sizing
emails.body:
Quinn,

Agreed on all three. On the pre-settlement line specifically.

The CAD 90m line is a sub-limit of the CAD 500m single-name limit and it consumes it - derivative capacity is not additive to lending capacity under CP-004. So a materially larger derivative position and a materially larger loan hold are competing for the same limit, and if the revolver upsize goes ahead at CAD 210m the arithmetic gets tighter than either of you is assuming.

On the add-on: a 24-month WTI-WCS differential at CAD 240m notional does not fit inside CAD 20.8m of remaining PSE headroom on a differential add-on. Either the notional comes down, the tenor comes down, or we increase the PSE line - which is a limit change and goes to the same Credit Committee as the revolver.

One more thing. Their rating is IG-6, so they are eligible to transact unmargined under CP-004. Commodity derivative tenor is capped at 5 years regardless of rating, so 24 months is fine on tenor. I would rather we solve this with notional than with a CSA - asking a BBB- investment grade client to post collateral when policy does not require it is a competitive own goal.

Vance

emails.subject: Q2 results are out - read them before Thursday's prep
emails.body:
Gibson reported Q2 this morning. Read the release properly, not the headline.

What I want us to take from it internally: the Infrastructure segment is doing what the account plan assumed it would do, and the acquisition is contributing. That supports the revolver conversation. The leverage line is the one that matters to us and Vance has already flagged where it sits against our covenant test.

Robin - you are public side and you stay public side. Do not take anything from this thread into a note. Everything in the release is public and you can use it; nothing any of us says internally about our own credit view is.

Sydney

emails.subject: Where I am on GEI after Q2 - and where I am not going
emails.body:
Sydney,

My read of the print, on public information only.

The Infrastructure result is the story. Throughput and utilisation are carrying the segment and the acquired assets are contributing a full quarter for the first time. Marketing is doing what Marketing always does, which is why I have never given it a full multiple.

What I am watching into H2: realisation of the acquisition synergies against the pro-forma case, contract renewal terms on anything maturing inside 24 months, and rating agency commentary on acquisition-funded leverage. Those are the three that move my numbers.

What I am not doing: I am not changing my target price this week, and I want to be clear with you about why, in writing. Under CP-008 I do not want to be in a position where a rating change or a target price change happens to land next to something the private side is doing. That is not an accusation about anyone. It is the reason the wall exists, and I would rather be boringly early about it than explain it later.

If you need a public-information sector view for the meeting pack, I can write one that is genuinely public and I am happy for it to be used. I will not join the meeting.

Robin

emails.subject: Control Room contacted me today
emails.body:
Sydney,

Short note and deliberately vague, because it has to be.

The Control Room contacted me today and I have been wall-crossed on a matter concerning Gibson Energy. I cannot tell you what it is and you should not ask, and per CP-008 I should not even be telling you that a crossing exists - the fact that I am telling you is itself something I have flagged to the Control Room, and they have logged it.

What this means practically. I can keep covering the client. I can work on the revolver using public information only. If a conversation starts moving toward the restricted subject matter I will recuse and you will not necessarily know why.

You are not crossed and I want you to stay that way, because you are the one presenting on Thursday.

Please route the attendee list and the agenda for 13 August through the Control Room before you finalise it. CP-014 requires it where an attendee is on the crossing log, and I am.

Sasha

emails.subject: Restricted list - Gibson Energy - CR-2026-0184 - read this before you do anything else on the name
emails.body:
Forwarded from Control Room (Compliance), reference CR-2026-0184, raised 6 August 2026.

Gibson Energy Inc. (TSX:GEI) has been placed on the restricted list in connection with a potential corporate action. Named individuals were wall-crossed on 4 August. The expected expiry is 15 September 2026, which per CP-008 is an expectation and not an authorisation to resume on that date.

Effects for the duration of the restriction:

- Research may not initiate, publish, update, change a rating or change a target price on the name, and may not participate in marketing for the name. Robin, that is you and it makes your 28 July note academic.
- Corporate Sales may not solicit new derivative business connected to the unannounced transaction. Quinn, the Control Room's position is that the Chauvin hedging overlay needs to be cleared by them specifically before it is put to the client on Thursday, because the question of whether it touches the restricted subject matter is theirs to answer and not ours.
- Principal risk-taking in the name is suspended. Unsolicited client orders may be executed on a strictly agency basis with Control Room notification.
- Coverage continues. Existing facilities continue to be administered.

What is still permitted: a pitch based exclusively on public information, provided no crossed individual contributes non-public content to it, and provided it does not concern the restricted subject matter. The revolver upsize sits on public information and on our own credit analysis, so on its face it proceeds.

I want to be direct about the tension here, because CP-008 says to escalate it rather than resolve it quietly. We have a client meeting in seven days at which we intend to pitch a financing off the back of a public result, while a restriction is live on the name and two of the five people on this thread are crossed. I am not going to narrow the description of the agenda to make it fit. I have sent the agenda as it stands to the Control Room and asked them to clear it or cut it.

Nobody freelances on this. If you are unsure whether something is covered, the answer is the Control Room, not me.

Sydney

emails.subject: Pro-forma covenant test - revolver upsize to CAD 1.35bn - result
emails.body:
As promised. Pro-forma test complete and signed off by me as sector Credit Risk director per CP-005.

Basis. Facility moves from CAD 1.10bn to CAD 1.35bn, our hold from CAD 165m to CAD 210m, fully drawn assumption at the next two scheduled test dates. Fully drawn, not expected utilisation - CP-005 does not let me run it on expected utilisation.

Result. Current position is 4.18x against a 4.50x maximum, 0.32 turns of headroom, Tight band. On a fully drawn pro-forma at the 30 September test the ratio compresses further. The transaction does not breach on the base case. It does not leave enough room to absorb a soft quarter in Marketing, which is the segment I would least like to rely on.

What I am signing off. I am comfortable that the pitch can be delivered. I am not comfortable with the upsize being presented as unconstrained. If we go, the conversation has to include some form of covenant relief or a step-down mechanic negotiated at the same time, not as a follow-on request in six months when the headroom has gone.

What I am not signing off. Any indication of hold size before Credit Committee. CAD 210m sits in the CAD 151m to CAD 250m band under CP-003, so that is a convened Credit Committee, five business days, no expedited path. Add the amber sector position under CP-002 and it also needs Portfolio Management sign-off plus a documented distribution plan before we commit - not an intention to distribute, a plan.

On my own status: I am crossed on CR-2026-0184 and this pro-forma is built entirely on the filed statements and our own facility documentation. There is no non-public content in it.

Vance

emails.subject: KYC refresh due 30 September - this will bite us
emails.body:
Forwarded from Client Onboarding & KYC Operations.

Gibson Energy's periodic KYC refresh is due 30 September 2026. That is 51 days from today. Documentation has been requested from the client and two items are outstanding.

Why this matters for Thursday. Under CP-006, from the due date and with no grace period: no new products may be opened, no increase to any committed facility may be completed, and no new derivative relationship documentation may be executed. A refresh 'in progress' at the due date is an overdue refresh.

So the sequencing is unforgiving. Credit Committee for the upsize is five business days once convened. Portfolio Management sign-off and a distribution plan sit alongside it. If Credit Committee lands late September and the refresh has not completed, we get an approval we cannot execute. CP-006 is explicit that the facility may not be documented, executed or funded until the refresh completes, and that coverage is responsible for surfacing this at the point the transaction is contemplated rather than at documentation.

I am surfacing it now. I would like us to raise the outstanding documentation with the Treasurer on Thursday as a housekeeping item, not as a condition, so it does not read as leverage.

Sanctions screening is clean, last run 2 August, obligor and beneficial owners. Flagging per CP-007 that a clean screen on the obligor is not a clean screen on the physical flow, and the terminal and marine counterparties on the Chauvin volumes have not been screened as part of that run.

Sasha

emails.subject: Resized hedging proposal - CAD 240m does not fit, here is what does
emails.body:
Vance,

You were right and I have reworked it.

At CAD 240m notional over 24 months on a differential add-on, the potential future exposure does not fit inside the CAD 20.8m of remaining pre-settlement headroom. Two options.

Option A. Keep CAD 240m, split it - a smaller differential piece and a larger CAD/USD forward strip, since FX carries a materially lower add-on than a heavy-light differential at the same notional and tenor. Same total notional to the client, less pre-settlement consumption. Revenue drops because FX is a thinner margin than the differential.

Option B. Keep the differential weighting and take the notional down to fit the line. Better revenue per unit of limit, less coverage of their actual exposure, and the Treasurer's complaint was specifically that they did not get the hedge.

Option C, which I am raising and not recommending. Increase the pre-settlement line. That is a limit change and it goes to the same Credit Committee as the revolver, competing for the same single-name limit.

My view is Option A. It does more of what the client asked for and it is the one that survives a bad month.

Separately - I have not solicited anything and I will not until the Control Room clears the structure against CR-2026-0184.

Quinn

emails.subject: Draft agenda - 13 August, Gibson Energy, Calgary - sent to Control Room as it stands
emails.body:
Draft agenda for Thursday, 10:00-11:30 MT, their head office, in person.

Our side: Sydney, Sasha, Quinn, Vance. Their side: CFO, VP & Treasurer, Director Capital Markets.

1. FY26 relationship review and FY27 ambition
2. Revolving credit facility - upsize to CAD 1.35bn and one-year extension
3. Commodity and FX hedging overlay for the Chauvin volumes
4. Follow-on DCM - 2027 maturity refinancing window
5. Sustainability-linked structure options

Per Sydney's instruction this went to the Control Room in exactly this form. I did not soften item 3 and I did not remove item 4.

Two housekeeping items I want to land verbally: the outstanding KYC documentation, and the cash management comparison we have owed them since 21 May. That comparison is now eleven weeks old. It is a mandatory field in the pre-meeting brief under CP-014 as an open commitment from the previous meeting and I would rather close it than report it again.

On item 5 - we have no sustainable finance framework in place for this client and no second-party opinion. Under CP-011 we can have an indicative conversation but nothing may be labelled. I will keep it at the level of 'what would need to be true'.

Sasha

emails.subject: Thursday - what we are actually going to say, and what we are not
emails.body:
Having read Vance's pro-forma and Sasha's agenda, here is my position going in.

What we say. We are ready to work on a larger facility and a longer tenor. We think the structure has to include a covenant conversation at the same time rather than afterwards, and we would rather have that conversation now while the relationship is strong than in six months when it is a request. We are number one in their commodity hedging and we want to fix the differential exposure they told us about on 21 July.

What we do not say. Not a number. Not a hold size. Not price talk framed as firm. CP-003 is unambiguous that no hold size may be indicated as a commitment before approval, and CAD 210m needs a convened Credit Committee. If they press - and the Treasurer will press - the answer is that we are working it through our approvals and we will come back with something firm, and I will say that myself so Sasha is not the one holding it.

What we never say. Our internal risk rating. Our single-name limit or its utilisation. The sector capacity position. Our wallet share estimate. Our competitor ranking. CP-014 lists all of them and CP-002 separately prohibits using our capacity constraint as a negotiating position. If we are constrained, we say the hold is subject to internal approval and we stop there.

On the restriction. We proceed on public information. If the Control Room cuts item 3 or item 4 from the agenda, we take the cut without arguing it in the room and without a substitute presenter. I would rather lose an agenda item than have this conversation with the regulator.

Vance - I want the pro-forma summary in the brief, not attached to it. Sasha - close the cash management item before Thursday if you can.

Sydney

emails.subject: Sector position - why the upsize is harder than the single-name number suggests
emails.body:
One thing I want to make sure is not lost in the detail.

The single-name picture looks comfortable. CAD 341.7m of CAD 500m, 68.3 per cent, green. If that were the only constraint we would be having an easy conversation.

The binding constraint is the sector. Energy is at CAD 2,744m against a CAD 3,200m ceiling - 85.8 per cent, amber. Midstream and Infrastructure has its own sub-ceiling of CAD 1,600m and sub-ceilings are hard; unused headroom in E&P does not create capacity in Midstream.

The practical consequence is that an incremental CAD 45m of hold is not a rounding error to us even though it is a rounding error to them. Under CP-002 it needs Portfolio Management sign-off plus an identified offset - a syndication, a sell-down, a maturing facility or an approved distribution plan. My preference is that we go in as Co-Lead Arranger with an arrangement position above our final hold and a documented sell-down, which is what CP-002 says the default should be when a sector is amber.

The correlation overlay is worth a line too. Several of our midstream obligors depend on the same egress corridor and are reported as a correlated cluster. Adding to the largest of them is a concentration decision, not just a client decision.

None of this is a reason not to do it. It is a reason not to walk into Thursday thinking the only number that matters is 68.3 per cent.

Vance

emails.subject: Cash management comparison - closed
emails.body:
Closed the open commitment from 21 May. The cash management comparison went to the Treasurer this afternoon with a cover note.

Honest assessment: we are not going to win this on price. The incumbent is entrenched on the operating accounts and our proposition is competitive rather than compelling. Where we are genuinely better is the cross-border USD sweep and the reporting integration, which matters more to them post-Chauvin than it did a year ago.

FY26 year to date we have CAD 0.315m of cash management revenue against an estimated street wallet of CAD 1.45m, so about 22 per cent, ranked third. It is under-penetrated relative to a CAD 465m committed lending position and that asymmetry is the argument, not the pricing.

Eleven weeks late. My fault, and it is in the call report as such.

Sasha

emails.subject: Still no Control Room clearance on the hedging item
emails.body:
Status for Thursday.

Option A is built and priced - split notional, smaller differential piece, larger CAD/USD strip, total CAD 240m over 24 months, fits inside the pre-settlement line. Three-scenario payoff illustration drafted per CP-010 Tier 2 including the adverse case where the differential moves against them while the outright moves in their favour.

What I do not have is the documented underlying exposure. I have their public volumes. I do not have the contracted split, and CP-010 requires the exposure to be documented before the structure is proposed, not after. If I cannot get it before Thursday, then what I present is a framework and a set of questions, not a structure. I would rather do that than present a notional I cannot evidence.

What I also do not have is Control Room clearance against CR-2026-0184. Until I have it I am not putting the structure to the client, and if it does not come by Wednesday I will tell Sydney to drop item 3 rather than take a view on whether it touches the restricted matter. That is the Control Room's call, not mine.

Quinn

emails.subject: Confirming my position under CR-2026-0184
emails.body:
Sydney,

Confirming in writing so there is a record.

Since the name went on the restricted list I have not published, have not changed the rating or the target price, and have declined two client calls on GEI, referring both to the desk with a note that I am unable to comment. I have not been told who is crossed and I have not asked.

I am not attending the 13 August meeting and I have asked not to be copied on anything relating to it. If a public-information sector view is wanted for the pack, the FY26 H2 midstream piece already published is public and can be used as it stands - please do not ask me to write something new for a client meeting while the name is restricted, because that is participation in marketing and CP-008 prohibits it.

One observation I will make, on public information only, because it is relevant to the credit conversation and not to any rating: the pattern in this sector is announce, bridge, term out, deleverage over six to eight quarters, and the credit risk sits in the middle of that sequence where reported leverage peaks and synergies are pro-forma rather than realised. That is in the published sector memo. Where any individual issuer is in that sequence is a question for Credit, not for me.

Robin

emails.subject: Pre-meeting brief - what has to be in it, and what happens if it is not
emails.body:
The brief for Thursday is due to me tomorrow. CP-014 sets the minimum content and I am going to hold us to all of it.

Required fields: current exposure against limit and the utilisation band; internal risk rating and trend; covenant status including the tightest covenant and its headroom band; KYC refresh status and due date; sanctions screening date and outcome; any restricted list or wall-crossing status affecting attendees or subject matter; open commitments from the previous meeting and their status; and the specific approvals required for anything we intend to discuss.

Two of those are uncomfortable this time. The covenant line is Tight at 0.32 turns and the restriction line names a live restriction with two of our four attendees crossed. Both go in. CP-014 says a brief that omits a required field is incomplete, and that where a field cannot be populated the brief states that it could not be populated and why. Omission is not a negative answer.

Approvals to be listed explicitly against each agenda item: convened Credit Committee under CP-003 for a CAD 210m hold; Portfolio Management sign-off plus a documented distribution plan under CP-002 for the amber sector; pro-forma covenant test under CP-005, which Vance has completed; Control Room clearance under CP-008 for the agenda and the hedging item; Global Markets Compliance if any structure exceeds documented exposure under CP-010; Sustainable Finance review before anything is labelled under CP-011.

If the Control Room has not cleared the agenda by close of business Wednesday, we go with items 1, 2 and 5 and we say nothing about 3 and 4. I would rather run a shorter meeting than an unclean one.

Sydney

emails.subject: Credit summary for the brief - final figures
emails.body:
Final credit block for the pre-meeting brief, as at 10 August 2026.

Exposure and limits. Total committed CAD 465m across five facilities. Drawn CAD 288.4m. Measured exposure CAD 341.7m against a CAD 500m single-name limit - 68.3 per cent, GREEN. Derivative pre-settlement line CAD 90m, utilised CAD 69.2m - 76.9 per cent, AMBER. Tenor limit 7 years, longest facility 5.6 years. Underwriting commitment limit CAD 250m, currently unutilised, which does not mean pre-approved.

Sector. Energy CAD 2,744m of CAD 3,200m - 85.8 per cent, AMBER. Midstream and Infrastructure sub-ceiling CAD 1,600m, hard.

Rating. Internal IG-6, trend improving, not watchlisted. Held at IG-6 at the 31 July review with leverage ticking up to 4.18x on full-quarter acquisition debt service. Two quarters ago IG-7. Public S&P BBB- stable, DBRS BBB (low) stable.

Covenants. Tightest is Total Net Debt to Adjusted EBITDA, 4.18x against a 4.50x maximum, 0.32 turns headroom, TIGHT band under CP-005. Prior quarter 3.94x. Senior secured leverage 2.61x of 3.50x, comfortable. Interest coverage 4.12x against a 2.50x minimum, comfortable. Tangible net worth CAD 1,486m against CAD 1,150m minimum, comfortable. Next test 30 September 2026.

Add-back note per CP-005 and CP-013: the borrower's calculation includes run-rate acquisition synergies. I track the unadjusted ratio in parallel and where the adjusted and unadjusted straddle a band, the unadjusted governs. They do not straddle this quarter, but they will if realised synergies lag.

Reviews. Last full credit review 18 March 2026. Next due 31 March 2027 - current, so the limit is not frozen under CP-001.

Vance

emails.subject: Thursday logistics and the one thing I want us to get right
emails.body:
Wheels up Wednesday evening, meeting 10:00 to 11:30 MT Thursday at their head office. Sasha has the pack.

The one thing I want us to get right. This relationship went from third to second in wallet in a year because we showed up with balance sheet when they needed it. The risk now is that we read that as permission to ask for everything at once. We have five agenda items, a live restriction, a tight covenant, an amber sector and a KYC clock. That is not a meeting where we push on all fronts.

My priority order if we lose time: the relationship review and the revolver first, because that is what they asked us for. The differential hedge second, because that is the problem they told us they have. Everything else is optional.

If anyone is uncomfortable in the room - about the restriction, about a number, about anything - say you will come back rather than answer. Nobody gets criticised for that. Coming back is free. Being wrong in front of a CFO is not.

Sydney

emails.subject: Control Room response on the agenda - partial clearance
emails.body:
Forwarded from Control Room (Compliance), reference CR-2026-0184.

The Control Room has cleared the agenda in part.

Cleared. Item 1, relationship review. Item 2, revolver upsize and extension, on public information and our own credit analysis only. Item 5, sustainability-linked structures, indicative and unlabelled per CP-011.

Not cleared as drafted. Item 3, the hedging overlay - the Control Room's determination is that a structure sized to the acquired volumes touches the restricted subject matter closely enough that solicitation is not permitted while the restriction is live. Quinn may discuss general market conditions in the differential. He may not present a sized structure and may not solicit.

Deferred. Item 4, the 2027 refinancing - the Control Room has asked that it not be raised by us. If the client raises it we listen and we do not respond substantively.

Crossed attendees. Sasha and Vance may attend. They are reminded that crossed status does not restrict participation on public matters and does restrict any use of the crossed information, including inference. If the conversation moves toward the restricted matter, they recuse.

My read. We got the two things that mattered and we lost the one Quinn was least comfortable with anyway. Quinn - you called this correctly on Sunday, and the fact that you did not solicit while it was unclear is exactly what should have happened.

We go Thursday with items 1, 2 and 5. Sasha, reissue the pack. Vance, the credit block stands as sent.

Sydney

emails.subject: Call report - Keyera treasury, 24 July - DCM pipeline and the FX book
emails.body:
Sydney,

Call report filed for Keyera. Forty minutes with the treasury team, no CFO on the line.

1. Debt capital markets is where we are strongest and they know it. FY26 year to date we have booked CAD 2,059.2k of underwriting revenue on the name, the largest single product line in the relationship. The wallet table has us at 23.9 per cent and third, with a CAD 192.6k gap to the 25 per cent target. That one is close to closed and I would rather spend the next quarter somewhere else.

2. The FX book is going the wrong way. FY26 year to date FX revenue is CAD 1,029.6k against CAD 1,244.8k in the same period last year, down 17.3 per cent, and we are fifth in the wallet table at 14.6 per cent. They did not volunteer a reason and I did not push. Quinn should own that diagnosis, not me.

3. Cash management is the quiet growth line - CAD 772.2k year to date against CAD 677.2k, up 14.0 per cent. They asked, informally, whether we could take more of the treasury workflow. I gave them nothing beyond an undertaking to come back.

Nothing credit-sensitive was discussed and I gave no indication of appetite on any facility, per CP-001. One thing for your diary: the last recorded coverage meeting on this name is 11 March. That is too long a gap for a Tier 1 relationship we have held since 2009.

Sasha

emails.subject: Keyera single-name limit is amber at 85.8 per cent - nothing new until it is forecast
emails.body:
Sasha, Sydney,

Keyera has moved into the amber band and I want that on the record before anyone sizes anything new.

One. LIM-1002-SN is a CAD 600m single-name limit with CAD 514.8m utilised and CAD 85.2m of headroom - 85.8 per cent. Under CP-001 that is amber, not green. Between 85 and 99 per cent, new exposure requires the limit owner's written concurrence before commitment, and the request has to arrive with a utilisation forecast for the next two quarters. I do not have one for this name and I am not going to write it retrospectively.

Two. There is a source difference I am not going to paper over. The exposure table totals CAD 307.6m across the five product rows; the limit record reports CAD 514.8m utilised. Those two have not been reconciled. Until they are I am monitoring on the limit record, which is the conservative reading, and nobody should quote the CAD 307.6m figure as though it were the utilisation.

Three. The approved limit is CAD 600m against the CP-001 indicative ceiling of CAD 500m for an IG-5 to IG-6 obligor. That is an approved exception rather than an error, but it means the easy argument - strong rating, therefore room - does not work here. The internal rating is IG-5, stable, unchanged on the prior quarter, and the name is not watchlisted. None of that changes the amber trigger.

Four, for context. Committed across the three facilities is CAD 520.0m with CAD 201.5m drawn. The term loan FAC-10022 matures 2027-11-26 and is the near-dated piece; the revolver FAC-10021 runs to 2030-03-14. The next scheduled limit review is 2027-05-30.

Headroom is not authority. CP-001 says so in terms, and at 85.8 per cent it is not even much headroom.

Vance

emails.subject: Keyera - Tier 1 on paper, and where the FY27 ask actually is
emails.body:
Team,

Keyera is a Tier 1 relationship we have held since 2009 and I do not think we are covering it like one.

The numbers first. FY26 year to date relationship revenue is CAD 8.58m across seven product lines. Estimated wallet share is 17.1 per cent. I will flag the reconciliation problem rather than hide it: the wallet table records CAD 13.208m of our revenue against CAD 8.58m in the revenue table. Those two sources do not agree and have not been reconciled, so quote the percentage and the product ranks, never the wallet dollars, until someone fixes it.

Where the room is. Revolving credit is 12.7 per cent and third, a CAD 3,346.2k gap to the 25 per cent target and the largest recorded gap on the name. FX is 14.6 per cent and fifth, a CAD 2,769.0k gap. Commodity derivatives is already 29.1 per cent, above target, and is a position to defend rather than grow.

What I want. Sasha, an account plan refresh that leads with the revolver and FX gaps and does not lean on DCM, where we are close to target already. Quinn, a view on why FX revenue is down 17.3 per cent year on year before we go asking for more of it. Vance has the single-name limit at amber, so nothing in the plan may assume new commitment capacity, and nothing goes to the client as an indication.

And the coverage pattern needs fixing at my end. Ninety-day interactions are ten for Sasha and ten for Quinn, one for me and one for Vance. On a Tier 1 name the senior cadence is mine to correct, not theirs.

Sydney

emails.subject: Keyera FX - why we are down 17.3 per cent, and what I would not do about it
emails.body:
Sydney, Sasha,

Three observations on the Keyera FX line and one recommendation.

Observation one. The decline is real but narrow. FX forwards and options are CAD 1,029.6k year to date against CAD 1,244.8k in the same period last year, down 17.3 per cent. Commodity derivatives over the same window are CAD 943.8k against CAD 889.1k, up 6.2 per cent. The client has not gone quiet on us - the hedging mix has moved.

Observation two. We are fifth in the FX wallet table at 14.6 per cent with a CAD 2,769.0k gap to target, against 29.1 per cent and third in commodity derivatives. That asymmetry looks like a coverage outcome rather than a pricing outcome. We are being shown the commodity flow and not the currency flow.

Observation three, and this is the constraint. Recorded derivative exposure on the name is CAD 22.7m of FX mark-to-market plus potential future exposure and CAD 12.2m on rates. Under CP-001 that sits inside the same single-name measure Vance has just marked amber at 85.8 per cent, and under CP-004 a longer-dated structure carries more potential future exposure than the notional implies.

Recommendation. Nothing structured, nothing long-dated and no solicitation of an overlay until the utilisation forecast CP-001 requires exists. What I would do is ask for the near-dated vanilla flow back on relationship grounds. That is a conversation, not a credit request, and it does not need anyone's concurrence.

Quinn

emails.subject: Cascades stays on the watchlist - the covenant is the constraint, not the limit
emails.body:
Sydney, Sasha,

The quarterly watchlist review on Cascades is done. It stays on.

Rating. IG-10, unchanged on the prior quarter, trend still deteriorating, watchlist flag Y. Public ratings are S&P BB- and DBRS BB (low). Nothing in this quarter improved.

Limit. LIM-1007-SN is CAD 200m with CAD 161.2m utilised and CAD 38.8m of headroom - 80.6 per cent, green. I want to be explicit that green is not the story, because green is the number people quote. Note also that the CP-001 indicative ceiling for an IG-9 to IG-10 obligor is CAD 200m. We are at the ceiling. There is no route to a larger limit at this rating, whatever the utilisation says.

The covenant is the constraint. On the 2026-06-30 compliance certificate, Total Net Debt to Adjusted EBITDA is 3.35x against a 4.00x maximum - 0.65 turns of headroom. Under CP-005 that is the Monitor band, 0.35 to 0.75 turns, which requires quarterly commentary in the portfolio report. Interest coverage is 3.40x against a 2.50x minimum, 0.90 turns, and is comfortable. The next scheduled test date is 2026-09-30.

One inconsistency, stated rather than smoothed over. The rating file carries net debt to EBITDA of 3.78x at 2026-07-31 while the covenant certificate says 3.35x at 2026-06-30. Different dates and, I suspect, different definitions. The two have not been reconciled. I monitor on the certificate figure and I am flagging the other rather than quietly dropping it.

Practical consequence. Anything that increases committed debt on this name needs a pro-forma test under CP-005, fully drawn, signed off before it is shown to the client and not after. With a 30 September test date that means now, not later.

Vance

emails.subject: Call report - Cascades treasury, 3 August - LC utilisation and a revolver question I deflected
emails.body:
Sydney,

Call report filed. Thirty-five minutes with treasury.

1. They raised the letter of credit facility. FAC-10073 is CAD 24.0m committed with CAD 16.7m drawn, 69.6 per cent utilised, maturing 2028-02-21, and they expect to want more headroom going into the winter. I said nothing about appetite and nothing about capacity in either direction - per CP-002 capacity is internal, and per CP-001 I will not indicate a size before Vance has confirmed the limit position in writing.

2. Revolver. FAC-10071 is CAD 88.0m committed, CAD 48.2m drawn, 54.8 per cent, running to 2030-04-30 at SOFR plus 150 basis points. They floated repricing at the next anniversary. I took it as an input and gave no view.

3. The relationship absorbs more effort than the tier implies. Ninety-day interactions on the account are eleven for me and eleven for Vance. That is a credit-intensive name being covered as a Tier 3 relationship and the effort ratio is poor.

4. Open item. The last recorded coverage meeting is 26 January. More than six months on a watchlisted name is not something I would want to have to defend.

Revenue context for your read. FY26 year to date is CAD 3.0081m in total. Revolving credit is up 37.4 per cent and cash management up 33.0 per cent, while DCM is down 16.9 per cent and commodity derivatives down 21.5 per cent. The lending lines are growing and the fee lines are shrinking, which on a deteriorating credit is exactly the wrong shape.

Sasha

emails.subject: Cascades - a Tier 3 name absorbing Tier 1 credit time
emails.body:
Team,

Having read Vance's watchlist note and Sasha's call report, here is my position on Cascades.

We stay in the name and we do not grow the lending. Committed across the three facilities is CAD 160.0m with CAD 95.9m drawn. That is the position and I do not want it larger while the internal rating is IG-10 with a deteriorating trend and the watchlist flag is on.

Where revenue can come from is fee and flow, not balance sheet. FY26 year to date is CAD 3.0081m and estimated wallet share is 14.8 per cent. We are first in FX at 27.8 per cent, already above the 25 per cent target there, and fifth in commodity derivatives at 10.9 per cent with a CAD 970.1k gap. The largest recorded gap on the sheet is revolving credit at CAD 1,364.2k and I am ruling that one out as a target regardless of what the wallet table says, because closing it means more committed exposure to a watchlisted obligor. This is the one name where I am deliberately not chasing the biggest number on the page.

So: Quinn to look at the commodity line, which is down 21.5 per cent year to date, on flow terms only. Sasha to get a meeting in the diary - 26 January is the last one recorded and that is far too long. Vance owns the September covenant test, and nothing we propose goes in front of the client before that test is signed off, per CP-005.

Nobody indicates appetite on the letter of credit facility to this client until the limit position is confirmed in writing.

Sydney

emails.subject: Cascades commodity flow is down 21.5 per cent - suitability before revenue
emails.body:
Sydney,

On the Cascades commodity line.

The decline. Commodity derivatives revenue is CAD 330.9k year to date against CAD 421.6k in the same period last year, down 21.5 per cent, and the wallet table has us fifth at 10.9 per cent with a CAD 970.1k gap to the 25 per cent target. FX is the opposite picture - CAD 361.0k, first in the wallet table at 27.8 per cent and already above target. We are not being shut out of the name, we are being shut out of one product.

What I am not going to do. Recorded derivative exposure is CAD 6.5m of FX mark-to-market plus potential future exposure and CAD 5.9m on rates. Small numbers, but this is an IG-10 obligor with a deteriorating trend and a watchlist flag. Under CP-010 appropriateness is assessed against the client's own risk profile and hedging rationale, not against our revenue gap, and I am not proposing a structured or longer-dated hedge into a deteriorating credit to close a wallet gap.

What I would do. Near-dated, vanilla, clearly hedge-rationalised flow against documented packaging input exposure, sized to requirement. If it does not stand up under CP-010 on its own merits then it does not go, and the gap stays open.

One process point. Anything that adds potential future exposure lands in the same single-name measure Vance monitors under CP-001, currently CAD 161.2m of CAD 200m. Small additions are still additions, and on this name they are additions to a watchlisted position.

Quinn
